_comment_family: New Order is a family and this file is its Medium, but like
korolev-bold it needs no care taken over the name: the file already
carries 'New Order Medium' as name ID 1, keeps the bare 'New Order'
in the typographic family (ID 16) with the cut in ID 17, and repeats
'New Order Medium' as the full name (ID 4). The family name and the
full name are the same string, so the name declared here is both, and
it answers with one cut whichever of the two a browser matches on.
That is the property the two Telegraf packs go to some trouble to buy
and this one gets for nothing, and it is worth having for their reason
even though nothing threatens it today. One cut of New Order is in
fonts/ and one channel is set in it, so there is no sibling a bare
family name could wrongly answer with - until the day a Bold arrives
beside it, which is a day this face should not have to be rewritten
Weight 500, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Stated rather than left to 'normal' so that the fallbacks
below resolve to a weight of their own family rather than to whatever
the browser picks when it is asked for nothing in particular.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and the second the
PostScript name (ID 6); both name this one cut rather than a family
with cuts in it, so a machine answering to either is answering with
The first is also the name the installer registers the face under - it
copies each pack's font into the user's font folder and keys it by
local[0] (see engine.install_fonts), and Windows keys installed fonts
by their full name. So this list being in this order is what makes the
installed copy findable by the stack below.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and here they were
chosen by measuring, because the channel set in this face draws a card
cut to each line's measured width: a substitute wider than the face
the lines were broken against does not make a different-looking
caption, it makes a card that overhangs the 90% column the block was
given.
New Order Medium is wide for its weight - a geometric with a round O
at 0.844em and a W at a full em - and that is unusual enough to be
worth a number. Its capitals average 0.620em, and twenty of them, which
is one caption line at the Snapchat preset's maxChars, come out at
496px against the 486px a line has. What the machine can be relied on
to have measures, at the same size: Segoe UI 490px, Arial 542px,
Impact 407px, Arial Black 615px.
So Segoe UI first, at 1.3% off, which is as close as a Windows machine
gets to anything and closer than this face has any right to expect.
Asked for at the declared 500 it resolves to the Regular, which is
what was measured - the family's next cut up is the Semibold at 600
and CSS weight matching looks down before it looks up. Arial behind
it, 9% wider and a caption that has lost a word off the end of a line
rather than a caption that has lost its face entirely.
Impact is absent, alone among the display faces in this folder that
carry it. It is 18% NARROWER, and the direction matters as much as the
distance: a face that undershoots does not overflow anything, it draws
a heavy condensed grotesque where a wide geometric medium should be,
which is the furthest thing on the machine from what this is. Arial
Black is absent for the ordinary reason - at 24% over, it is not a
fallback but a guarantee of a card wider than the column.
